To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The dorsal visual processing system, in isolation from ventral stream information, influences the identification of objects, 2) The dorsal system does not compute function-specific information, and 3) The influence of the dorsal system on object identification is not specific to functionally relevant objects.
1) The dorsal visual processing pathway, in isolation from other visual pathways, can influence the selection of both superordinate and basic level object labels.
1) the dorsal visual processing system is involved in tool identification, and 2) the dorsal system does not carry function specific information about tools.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dorsal stream structures in the visual recognition of objects, and how information computed by these structures influences decisions about object identity.
the interaction between the dorsal and ventral visual processing streams and the influence that the former has on the identification of manipulative objects.
how visual processing of object identity is influenced by the processing of object function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dorsal stream does indeed influence the identification of objects, but it does so in a manner that is agnostic as regards the specific identity of those objects.
the dorsal stream is not about object identity, but rather it is about the motor relevant properties of the objects that we manipulate.
information computed by dorsal structures is not about the identity of objects, but is about the action that the object is used for.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
information from the dorsal stream is not about object identity, but about motor relevant properties of manipulable object.
dorsal stream structures are agnostic to object identity, but are sensitive to the manipulability of objects, and that this sensitivity is not function specific.
the dorsal stream computes object related information that is not about the identity of the object, nor is it function specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
information originating in the dorsal stream influences object recognition, and that this information is not about the function or functional properties of the objects.
information computed by structures within the dorsal stream is not specific to a single object or object category.
dorsal stream structures can influence object identification in a functionally agnostic manner.
